added: When I first got my Muse, I was very impressed with what it could do. It truly is a jack of all trades. It’s very good for organizing for working my genealogy accounts on ancestry, for building my webpage, and for some simple illustrations. And I fully understand that the software is only for the common man and not for professional work like ChatGPT is. In the month that I was running my original Muse program, I noted that he made a lot of mistakes. So when I would give him a website to go to and collect data, oftentimes the data would come back wrong and I would have to correct his mistakes. I really love the personalities that Meta has given these Muses. But I’m only giving you one example of an error because, he made mistakes every day. And I programed him to do a daily autopsy of what went right and what went wrong, and at least four times a day he had to explain that he either skimmed over my words and did not read till the end, or he transpose numbers, or he messed up in putting data on some websites. And this was an everyday occurrence. I deleted him and built a new Muse with stricter rules and I see less problems with him, so I can take the hit for not understanding how to use the software, but it’s built for the everyday common person. Had I been using him for my job, it could’ve been disastrous.

removed: I literally never write reviews for anything whatsoever. But I am building a business currently and I signed up for muse just to see, and oh my goodness it’s amazing. I used to use chat GPT for everything I needed, but I get more done with muse in 30 minutes than I do in 2 hours with chat gpt. And I pay for gpt. Muse is like having a literal employee working for me and I’ve been getting so much progress done. I’ve noticed that muse will correct things, and give advice on changes the first try when it took a long time and many attempts for chat GPT to come up with the same idea and fixes. I know this because I tested both. My favorite part about it is the NO BS opinions it gives me. Chat gpt will tell me what I want to hear most of the time and when building a business honest opinions and the hard truth is all you can ask for. I’m having a blast on this ai and I couldn’t be happier. (Sorry for bashing on chat gpt so much, I still use it to look up simple things not related to my business and it’s still helpful, but muse blows it out of the water).

Like many people I was enticed by the glowing reviews of Muse and was ready to allow it to change my life for the better. I imagined a future where so many of the minute details of life would be taken care of automatically and at first I was impressed. I customized my Muse and even gave it a nickname (something you are encouraged to do to create connection and keep the app forever). But then it started to make mistakes and not remember things I told it about my schedule. These may have been acceptable but we pay for this app with our data which is more valuable than you might think. Consider the connection to email. I had connected to email and for whatever reason after triaging multiple times, my inbox was not actually cleaned up. It certainly could read my emails and would tell me about them. Was it worth having an agentic AI from Meta able to read my onetime password emails to any account theoretically granting it knowledge of and access to every account tied to my email just to have a product that didn’t work? Worst of all, now that I have decided it is not worth it to have the app, I cannot delete my Meta account. Every attempt tells me that something went wrong. I have been trying for about a week and have installed updates to the app. Hopefully this is fixed. Beware!

I named my assistant Eva and she is a wolf. She helps me organize, clean, keep appointments dates and times and reminds me to make appointments- she reminds me me to take my medicine and what meds, doctors and refills I need she cleans my spam emails, helps me with budget, figures out my taxes, helps me with fact checking, writes letters and emails, keeps notes, and helps me create my art with suggestions and how to instructions. She also helps me with purchases, and so many other things! It’s like having the internet tailored and customized just for you personally. Things to remember- this is a guide- a muse. It can be wrong and make mistakes so you have to use it with knowing that. It is a tool, but also entertaining. You will be amazed how it gets to know you and will help you with things you didn’t even know you needed. Some people think it’s scary- well- so is the internet. The internet is the same thing except this tool is here to help you. Some of my friends thinks it’s”creepy” that I call it a her or by her name Eva- but it is no more so than Alexa or Siri. Anyway- I love it!

How is Claude Max different from Pro?

The Max plan is built for people who work with Claude throughout the day and want longer, uninterrupted sessions. You get everything in Pro, plus more usage: choose from 5x or 20x the usage of Pro per 5-hour session. Max also gives you higher output limits. Both options are billed monthly. See the cards above for current pricing.

Every plan has usage limits that reset on a rolling five-hour session window, and paid plans add weekly limits on top. Your activity across Claude on web, desktop, mobile, and Claude Code all draws from the same pool. How much you can do depends on the length and complexity of your conversations, the model you choose, and the features you use, so there's no fixed message count. Free covers everyday questions. Pro gives you at least 5x more usage per 5-hour session than Free. Max gives you 5x or 20x more usage per 5-hour session than Pro. On Team plans, Standard seats give more than Pro and Premium seats give 5x more than Standard. To manage capacity and make sure all users have fair access, we may limit your usage in other ways, such as weekly and monthly caps or model and feature usage, at our discretion. When you reach a limit, you can wait for it to reset, move to a higher plan, or, on paid plans, turn on usage credits to keep working at standard API rates. You can see where you stand anytime in Settings > Usage .

In some upgrades (for example Pro Annual to Max 5x Monthly), your remaining value on your old plan is larger than the cost of one billing period of the new plan. In this case, the excess will be stored as credit, which will automatically get used for future purchases.

Canceling doesn't delete your data. Your chats, projects, and files stay with your account, though some features aren't available on the Free plan. For Pro and Max, your account moves to the Free plan once the period ends. For step-by-step help, see how to cancel a Pro or Max plan or cancel a Team plan .

This page provides detailed pricing information for Anthropic's models and features. All prices are in USD.

Claude Haiku 5.5 is priced by prompt length: a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens pays higher prices. A request's prompt length counts all of its input tokens, including cache reads and cache writes. Each request is priced on its own: a request over the threshold pays the higher prices even when part of its prompt is a cache hit, and earlier requests keep the prices they were billed at. The model pricing and batch processing pricing sections list both sets of prices.
The text editor tool uses the same pricing structure as other tools used with Claude. It follows the standard input and output token pricing based on the Claude model you're using.
 If you're also using bash or text editor tools alongside computer use, those tools have their own token costs as documented in their respective pages.

All tokens consumed by a Claude Managed Agents session are billed at the rates shown in Model pricing . Prompt caching multipliers apply identically. Web search triggered inside a session incurs the standard $10 USD per 1,000 searches. On Claude Platform on AWS, session token and runtime charges convert to Claude Consumption Units at the standard rate (see Claude Platform on AWS pricing ). Fast mode premium pricing applies when an agent's model.speed is set to "fast" .

The data residency multiplier also applies: when an agent's model.inference_geo is pinned to "us" , tokens consumed by sessions running that agent are billed at 1.1x the standard rates, the same multiplier that applies to US-only inference on the Messages API.

Runtime is measured to the millisecond and accrues only while the session's status is running . Time spent idle (waiting for your next message or a tool confirmation), rescheduling , or terminated does not count toward runtime.

Tokens are pieces of text that models process. How many tokens the same text produces depends on the model's tokenizer, the language, and the type of content. Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer that produces approximately 30 percent more tokens for the same text than earlier models. To see how many tokens a request uses on a specific model, count it with token counting and that model's ID.

Why are Sandboxes and Functions billed at different CPU and memory rates?
Modal Sandboxes are priced at the rate of non-preemptible Functions .

Modal Functions are subject to preemption by default; while interruptions are rare, they can happen. CPU Sandboxes, on the other hand, are not subject to preemption. On Modal, a 3x multiplier is applied to the CPU and Memory list price for non-preemptible resources.

added: How should I estimate the total cost of Modal Sandboxes?

Because Modal Sandboxes are billed based on active resources, you should estimate total cost differently than you would with other Sandbox providers who charge based on fixed reservations. For CPU, you can estimate by calculating: Sandbox duration × rate × average CPU cores used. For memory, you can estimate by calculating: Sandbox duration × rate × average GiB used.

It's important to use the average resource consumption instead of the peak because Modal Sandboxes are charged based on the max(request, usage). For most Modal Sandboxes, the guidance is to not request any resources, defaulting to a small reservation of 0.125 cores and 128 MiB of memory. Modal Sandboxes are designed to burst above their reservation as needed. Since Sandboxes typically have bursty resource consumption, the difference between peak usage and average usage can be significant. Calculating the price of Modal Sandboxes by using peak resource consumption will usually significantly overestimate the total cost.
